{{Short description|Canadian-American statistician (1923-2001)}}
'''Ralph Allan Bradley''' (November 28, 1923 – October 30, 2001) was a Canadian-American statistician and statistics educator, whose research lay in the fields of [[design of experiments]], [[nonparametric statistics]], [[sequential analysis]], and [[Multivariate Analysis|multivariate analysis]]. He is known for the [[Bradley–Terry model]] in [[Pairwise comparison (psychology)|pairwise comparison]]<ref>{{Citation |last=Bradley |first=Ralph A. |chapter=14 Paired comparisons: Some basic procedures and examples |date=1984 |chapter-url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0169716184040165 |title=Handbook of Statistics |volume=4 |pages=299–326 |access-date=2023-08-19 |series=Nonparametric Methods |publisher=Elsevier |doi=10.1016/s0169-7161(84)04016-5|isbn=978-0-444-86871-8 |chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref> and for founding the Department of Statistics at [[Florida State University]].<ref name=interview>{{Cite journal |last1=Hollander |first1=Myles |last2=Bradley |first2=Ralph A. |date=2001 |title=A Conversation with Ralph A. Bradley |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2676781 |journal=Statistical Science |volume=16 |issue=1 |pages=75–100 |doi=10.1214/ss/998929483 |jstor=2676781 |issn=0883-4237}}</ref><ref name=obituary>{{Cite web |last=Hollander |first=Myles |title=Ralph Allan Bradley 1923-2001 |url=https://ani.stat.fsu.edu/newsletter/Fall2001.pdf}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Bradley was born in [[Smith Falls, Ontario|Smiths Falls, Ontario]], Canada and grew up in [[Wellington, Ontario]]. He studied mathematics and physics at [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]], receiving an honors degree in 1944. After a stint in the [[Canadian Army]], he returned to Queen's University and obtained an MA in 1946. He received his PhD in theoretical statistics in 1949 at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] under the supervision of [[Harold Hotelling]].

Bradley was employed at [[McGill University]] from 1949 to 1950 and as a faculty member at [[Virginia Tech]] from 1950 to 1958. In 1959, he moved to [[Florida State University]] to found the Department of Statistics there and stayed on until 1978 as the head of the department. In 1982, he moved to the [[University of Georgia]] as Research Professor of Statistics. Bradley retired from the [[University of Georgia]] in 1992. He continued to participate in research activities afterward and was named professor emeritus at both [[Florida State University]] and [[University of Georgia|the University of Georgia]].<ref name=interview /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ralph Allen Bradley |url=https://www.oxfordreference.com/display/10.1093/oi/authority.20110803095523418 |access-date=2023-08-19 |website=Oxford Reference |language=en  }}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
Bradley was editor of the journal [[Biometrics (journal)|Biometrics]] from 1957 to 1962. He was Vice-President from 1975 to 1978 and President in 1981 of the [[American Statistical Association]]. Bradley was a Fellow of the American Statistical Association and a Fellow of the Institute of Mathematical Statistics.<ref name=obituary /> The statistics department of the [[University of Georgia]] organizes an annual lecture in his name.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-02-24 |title=The 2023 Bradley Lecture |url=https://www.niss.org/events/2023-bradley-lecture |access-date=2023-08-19 |website=National Institute of Statistical Sciences |language=en}}</ref> In 1992 Bradley was awarded the [[American Statistical Association Founders Award|American Statistical Association's Founders Award]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Founders Award | publisher=American Statistical Association | url=https://www.amstat.org/your-career/awards/founders-award }}</ref>
